title: Towards Closing the Performance Gap for Cryptographic Kernels Between CPUs and Specialized Hardware
problem: Achieving near-ASIC performance for cryptographic kernels (Number Theoretic Transform, NTT; and large-integer BLAS operations) on commodity x86 CPUs remains an open challenge; current CPU baselines lag ASICs by orders of magnitude for these workloads, which are foundational to post-quantum cryptography and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE).
motivation: Post-quantum cryptography deployments require NTT and large-integer BLAS at high throughput, and while ASICs dominate, their inflexibility and deployment cost motivate finding how close general-purpose CPUs can get with careful ISA and microarchitecture investment.
method: The researchers built optimized x86-64 CPU code for NTT and large-integer BLAS (which perform arithmetic on very large numbers), then applied SIMD vectorization—a technique where the CPU processes multiple data points in parallel using AVX2 and AVX-512 instructions—to reach 38x and 62x speedups respectively over the previous best CPU implementations. They found that specialized cryptographic chips (ASICs) still outperform CPUs because they have hardware built-in for multi-precision modular arithmetic (the core mathematical operations in these algorithms), so they designed MQX: a small x86 extension that adds three instructions targeting these operations. MQX reduces the per-core gap to 35x, and their analysis shows that when large server CPUs with MQX use multiple cores, they can approach ASIC-level performance.
key_novelty: MQX, an x86 extension adding three AVX-512 instructions for multi-precision modular arithmetic (the large-number mathematical operations at the core of cryptographic algorithms), closes most of the remaining performance gap between standard CPUs and specialized cryptographic chips for NTT and large-integer BLAS.
contributions: Optimized scalar and AVX2/AVX-512 SIMD implementations of NTT and large-integer BLAS achieving 38x and 62x speedup over CPU baselines
MQX: a minimal 3-instruction AVX-512 extension targeting multi-precision modular arithmetic that reduces ASIC slowdown to 35x per core
Roofline analysis showing MQX-equipped multi-core server CPUs can approach ASIC-class throughput for cryptographic workloads
Characterization of the CPU-to-ASIC performance gap for NTT and BLAS cryptographic kernels with practical implications for FHE/PQC deployment

metrics.speedup: 38x over CPU baseline for NTT; 62x for BLAS (with AVX-512); ASIC slowdown reduced to 35x per core with MQX

baselines: State-of-the-art CPU baselines for NTT and BLAS
limitations: MQX requires hardware ISA changes not yet available in production silicon; multi-core scaling analysis is based on roofline projections rather than measured results on deployed hardware.
primary_theme: Closing CPU-to-ASIC performance gap for cryptographic kernels via SIMD and minimal ISA extension
